chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man in ihram who looked at non-mahram women and ejaculated; he said: 'Upon him is the sacrifice of a camel or a cow; if he cannot find [one], then a sheep.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever looked at his wife and ejaculated or emitted pre-seminal fluid, there is no expiation upon him, and he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted.

key_terms.غَيْرِ أَهْلِهِ: Non-mahram women (those permissible to marry but not currently married to)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of ihram (ritual consecration) for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man in ihram who looks at non-mahram women and ejaculates?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a graduated fidya system for a muhrim who gazes at non-mahram women and ejaculates, prescribing a camel, cow, or sheep based on financial capacity. Al-Tusi’s commentary clarifies that this penalty is specific to the act of looking at others, whereas looking at one's own wife with ejaculation incurs no fidya, requiring only istighfar, highlighting the distinction between minor and major breaches of ihram conditions.
